mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions and French domestic Tracfin alerts; PEP status assessed in accordance with Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Code monétaire et financier Art. L.561-10; enhanced due diligence triggered by PEP or sanctioned-country nexus. Ongoing monitoring via the national RCS/UBO registry and public procurement debarment lists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Infogreffe portal (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and INPI data portal (https://data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in French or transliterated into Latin script; non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew) require a recognised Latin transliteration; the name must be readable and pronounceable under French law and comply with the standards of the French name-availability check (Appréciation de disponibilité).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/Greffe rejects the proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request within 15 days of notification to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; if rejected after reconsideration, the applicant may appeal to the President of the Commercial Court in chambers (référé) or file a substantive application before the Commercial Court. A new name may be filed immediately without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted under Code de commerce Art. L.123-11-2 via approved domiciliation companies; valid for up to 5 years and renewable. For steel-structure prefab EPC projects, a virtual office is permissible for incorporation and tax registration, but physical presence is recommended for operating permits and tender accreditation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, principally Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and L.210-1 to L.210-9; incorporation filings under Articles R.123-1 et seq.; beneficial-ownership disclosure under Articles L.561-46 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce), with registration data maintained in the Registre National des Entreprises by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle through the mandatory Guichet unique des formalités.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a legal entity submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, together with the signed SAS articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and supporting documents; the filing results in registration in the Registre National des Entreprises and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; capital may be set at EUR 1 or more. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited in a blocked account with a bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and released after presentation of the K-bis registration extract. In-kind contributions require valuation by a commissaire aux apports unless a statutory exemption applies. The amount stated excludes publication, beneficial-owner filing, registry, professional, and banking charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders and appointed officers resolve that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription of its shares in the amounts and by the persons recorded in the subscription schedule, subject to receipt of all required contributions; (2) the registered office is established at the address stated in the articles of association; (3) [Name] is appointed President for the term and remuneration specified in the articles or appointment instrument; (4) [Name] is appointed General Director, if applicable; and (5) the President is authorized to complete all Guichet unique, registry, tax, banking, employment, and licensing formalities required for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the corporate name and verify the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI trademark database, Registre National des Entreprises, and the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed name for corporate and trademark conflicts. Secure a compliant registered-office address through owned premises, a commercial lease, domiciliation agreement, or qualifying home-office arrangement. Obtain a dated occupancy document and confirm that the premises permit the intended administrative activity.
required_dossiers: Domiciliation agreement or lease, if applicable
Identity and contact details of shareholders and officers
Business activity description and relevant NAF classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace the conflicting name, correct the address evidence, or provide an additional domiciliation document. If the filing portal rejects the formal submission, preserve the electronic rejection notice and resubmit with the identified defect cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution before submission to the Guichet unique; notarial intervention only where required by the transaction or contributed asset
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the articles of association in French or with a reliable French translation. State the name, legal form, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, share rights, transfer restrictions, governance rules, President, and accounting year. Obtain powers of attorney where signatories act through representatives. Notarization is generally not required for ordinary SAS articles, but signatures and translations should be formally certified when requested for foreign shareholders or public authorities.
required_dossiers: Cash contribution certificate or deposit certificate
Foreign shareholder corporate extracts and legalized powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct missing mandatory clauses, obtain replacement signatures, and cure translation, legalization, or contribution-valuation defects before resubmission. If an in-kind contribution exemption is used, retain the shareholder resolution documenting the exemption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal of Legal Notices (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed incorporation notice containing the corporate name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, President, and registry details. Use the journal's electronic or prescribed form and obtain the publication certificate. The legal notice must be published before the registration application is finalized.
required_dossiers: Final signed articles or incorporation particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice where information is inaccurate or incomplete and upload the replacement certificate. Ensure the notice is published in the correct department and within the applicable filing sequence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the electronic incorporation and beneficial-owner filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI, transmitting the file to the competent Greffe du tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic formalities account, select company creation, complete the SAS form, upload signed documents, identify all beneficial owners, pay applicable portal and registry charges, and electronically sign the filing. State the actual industrial activity and premises where operations will occur. Retain the submission receipt and reference number.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate documents with required legalization or apostille and French translation
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the Greffe query within the stated deadline through the portal, replace defective documents, pay any assessed balance, and resubmit the corrected file. For a refusal, request the formal grounds and use the applicable recourse before the competent court or registry authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration governance and operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIE business tax office, URSSAF, INSEE, commercial bank, and relevant local or industrial authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and verify the K-bis extract, activate the bank account, record the share ledger and beneficial-owner register, establish accounting records, and register as an employer before hiring. Confirm VAT and corporate-tax positions with the SIE. Before physical operations, verify planning, building, environmental, fire, occupational-safety, and waste requirements for the specific premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct post-registration data through the Guichet unique or the relevant authority, file late registrations promptly, and document any request for correction. Do not commence regulated physical operations until the applicable premises approvals or environmental filings are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Préfet of the department, supported by the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), for classified installations; the local mairie or intercommunal planning authority for planning and building controls. No general manufacturing licence is required solely for engineering design and assembly of prefabricated steel buildings.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating licence; where the facility falls within the nomenclature of Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE), the applicable instrument is an ICPE déclaration, enregistrement, or autorisation préfectorale, including any prescribed operating requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, with the competent Regional Environmental Authority (Mission Régionale d'Autorité environnementale) and DREAL services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening. Ordinary steel cutting, forming, welding, and assembly is not automatically subject to a full EIA. Surface treatment, painting, combustion, storage, waste, or other processes may trigger ICPE declaration, registration, authorization, or case-by-case environmental assessment under the Environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE order or prefectural permit, including limits for wastewater pollutants, suspended solids, metals, pH, noise, dust, and VOCs from coating operations. Classify and track hazardous waste, use licensed carriers and treatment facilities, prevent soil contamination, maintain spill controls, and meet applicable air-emission and waste-traceability requirements. No single universal threshold applies without the identified ICPE headings, equipment capacities, substances, and site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain planning or building permission where construction, change of use, floor area, structure, or external works require it. Confirm fire prevention measures with the mairie and, where applicable, the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours; obtain an ERP safety opinion or opening authorization if the premises receive the public. Commission structural design and load compliance under applicable French construction standards. Complete workplace risk assessment, machinery conformity, guarding, electrical and lifting-equipment inspections, occupational-health arrangements, emergency procedures, and required signage before production.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – French tax administration; business registration and related filings via www.impots.gouv.fr and the online corporate formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated SAS obtains a SIREN/SIRET identification from INSEE via the formalities portal on incorporation; the VAT number (n° d'identification TVA intracommunautaire) is attributed automatically by DGFiP once the business registration is transmitted. Non-resident companies not established in the EU that need to charge French VAT must apply for direct VAT registration with the DGFiP's non-resident VAT office (service des impôts des entreprises 'Paris-Étranger') or appoint a French tax representative established in the EU where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SAS is compulsorily subject to French corporate income tax ('impôt sur les sociétés') under CGI art. 206; no pass-through regime is available; profits are taxed at the entity level and distributions are separately subject to withholding/personal income tax.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists for French SAS entities. Optional regimes include: (1) tax consolidation under CGI art. 223 A for ≥95% French subsidiaries; (2) reduced corporate tax rates for certain SMEs on the first tranche of profit; (3) elections applicable under the ATAD hybrid rules (art. 209-0 B and related provisions) requiring, inter alia, notifications or recharacterisations of reverse hybrids and foreign branch mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No hard registration threshold exists for established French taxable persons; any independent economic activity is registrable for VAT. However, taxable persons may benefit from the art. 293 B CGI small-business exemption during a calendar year where turnover (previous year or current year annualised) is below EUR 93,100 for supplies of goods or EUR 38,500 for services (2025 scale).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B e-invoicing is mandatory for all French-established taxable persons under the 2020 e-invoicing reform: from 1 September 2026 every operator must receive structured e-invoices and large/medium enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027 small and medium enterprises must issue them. E-invoices must be transmitted through an accredited dematerialisation partner (PDP) or the public invoicing portal (PPF), and invoice data (e-reporting) is passed to DGFiP; France uses the 'Y' model without per-invoice notch/clearance stamp. There is no permanent real-time fiscal clearance obligation; electronic signature/stamp is not required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union are VAT zero-rated under CGI art. 262-I-1° provided that the goods are physically exported and the exporter obtains and holds proof of exit within the statutory period. Services directly connected to exported goods (e.g. freight, handling, customs clearance) can also be zero-rated under Article 262-I-4° for exports. For supplies of prefabricated steel structures, a supply that includes transport and installation outside the EU should be examined to distinguish a zero-rated sale of goods from a service to immovable property in the destination country; mixed contracts must be dissected under the VAT place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU with MRN - Movement Reference Number issued by French customs)
Commercial Invoice and signed contract or purchase order
Bill of Lading (B/L) or CMR consignment note, air waybill, or multimodal transport document
Packing list and loaded container details
Proof of exportation (e.g. export cargo summary / D.E.S. or Exit Summary Declaration) and electronic customs archives
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank transfer/LC settlement evidence proving receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT zero-rating is a high-risk audit area. If DGFiP determines that the export evidence package is incomplete or false, the tax authority reassesses the VAT at 20%, adds French late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) and applies penalties under CGI arts. 1728-1729-1732: 40% for deliberate misdeclaration, 80% for abuse of law/fraud; interest runs from the point of collection. In addition, unsupported 'zero-rating' on an invoice may trigger a client recapture under the invoice issuer joint liability rules and, in criminal cases, tax fraud sanctions under art. 1741 CGI. Exporters must retain all documentation for 6 years and present it on demand to the customs ('service des douanes') or DGFiP; failure to repatriate proceeds within the 180-day foreign-exchange deadline also exposes the company to financial trade sanctions under the Monetary and Financial Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking supervision and with the DG Trésor (Direction Générale du Trésor, French Treasury and Financial Sanctions Directorate) for foreign-exchange control, restrictive-measures enforcement and balance-of-payments reporting policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full currency convertibility as an eurozone EU Member State; Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital and payments. Current-account and capital-account flows are fully liberalised with no exchange-approval licences required for dividend/profit remittance, capital reductions, or repayment of shareholder advances. Residual hurdles are limited to: (i) mandatory Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration for any cross-border settlement or position exceeding EUR 12,500; (ii) compliance with EU/UN financial sanctions and asset-freeze lists; (iii) French corporate-law solvency tests before dividend distribution (French Commercial Code art. L232-11, including the half-year liquidity and net-assets test); and (iv) arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation for related-party profit remittances. No de jure restrictions on foreign shareholding exist for a French SAS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export-proceeds surrender regime: there is no statutory repatriation timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in foreign-currency or EUR accounts held at ACPR-licensed credit institutions, subject solely to reporting cross-border transactions or net positions exceeding EUR 12,500 to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. Under French GAAP, foreign-currency export receivables must be remeasured at closing-date spot rates, with unrealised exchange differences recognised in profit or loss; hedging thereof is freely permissible. EU dual-use and customs export declarations apply to steel-structure prefabricated goods under HS chapters 7308 and 9406 but do not condition or otherwise restrict FX conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for low-value operational disbursements; Low for capital-escrow, documentary-credit issuance and structural trade finance. EU/EEA-licensed e-money and payment institutions may passport into France under PSD2 and open remote EUR accounts (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Revolut Business holding a French or EU licence), but most impose monthly turnover ceilings, reject construction/EPC counterparties under enhanced KYC, and cannot issue letters of credit or provide blocked-warranty accounts acceptable to international counterparties. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs (UK post-Brexit, Singapore, or US fintechs) hold no passporting right; their use as primary rails exposes the SAS to unlicensed-banking risk under French Monetary and Financial Code art. L311-2. Recommended architecture: a Tier-1 French bank as master treasury, escrow and LC rail; a PSD2-passported French EMI as secondary rail only for vendor micro-payments below EUR 50,000 per month and not subject to documentary-credit terms.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A French SAS with non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners must expect mandatory physical presence of the legal representative (SAS Président) at account opening with Tier-1 French banks, particularly for capital-escrow and LC facilities. Remote opening is granted only where the director is an EEA resident with a certified eIDAS digital identity and the bank accepts supervised video onboarding, which remains exceptional for non-resident UBO structures. The accepted alternative is physical attendance of a French resident representative holding a notarised power-of-attorney issued by the SAS, coupled with live video verification of the director. The KYC interview on UBO structure and source of funds is non-waivable. Post-Brexit UK directors receive no preferential treatment and are treated as third-country nationals, requiring enhanced corroboration of identity and address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident multi-layer UBO chain — offshore parent above French SAS obscuring ultimate ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO declaration on the French ACPR/AMF template; certificate of incumbency, certificate of good standing and corporate registration extract for each holding layer; legalised or apostilled passport copies; residential address proof (utility bill or tax notice under 6 months); source-of-wealth statement; consolidated group organisational chart; and tax residence certificates of all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection or shareholder loan occurring shortly after incorporation with no prior operating track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAS deed of capital contribution / capital-increase deliberation duly signed; shareholder current-account (compte courant d'associé) agreement stating maturity, interest rate and repayment terms; originator bank statements evidencing cleared funds; board-approved business plan with procurement pipeline, capex budget and 24-month cash-flow forecast; and evidence of ultimate fund source, including sale proceeds, accumulated group EBITDA, inheritance or gift declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty geography intersecting EU restrictive-measures or high-risk jurisdiction lists in steel procurement or prefab sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU consolidated financial sanctions file and OFAC/World-Check/refinitiv screening reports covering all counterparties; end-user and beneficial-owner attestations from each supplier and buyer; ICC-compliant sales and procurement contracts with governing law and territorial application clauses; dual-use and customs classification confirmation for HS 7308 and 9406 demonstrating no-licence status; and bank-facilitated pre-transaction sanctions clearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-form mismatch: USD/CAD invoicing against EUR domestic costs, third-party payment routing, or advance-payment concentration in EPC contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month treasury and FX exposure forecast; signed proforma and final commercial invoices; SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment trail with matching purpose codes; bills of lading, CMR and customs declarations evidencing physical trade flows; UCP600-compliant LC documentation where applicable; and written narrative explaining currency selection, payment timing and beneficiary logic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-tripping payments to director-connected suppliers or related-party service providers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French transfer-pricing documentation per Commercial Code art. L13 AA, including benchmarking analysis; supplier due-diligence file comprising Kbis extracts, audited financial statements and ownership charts; signed contracts with delivery milestones evidenced by project photographs, customs clearances and installation certificates; and Banque de France foreign-direct-investment code filings for any intra-group cross-border flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) open a dedicated French capital-escrow or blocked account ('apport en compte bloqué') at an ACPR-licensed Tier-1 bank; (2) instruct the foreign parent to send a SWIFT MT103 wire referencing the SAS SIREN/Kbis number and the capital-filing reference in field 70, with French balance-of-payments purpose code S110 for equity contributions or ISO 20022 purpose 'INVC'/'COST' for loan advances; (3) for shareholder loans, use purpose code S112 accompanied by the signed loan agreement, interest-rate terms and repayment schedule; (4) report the inflow to the Banque de France through the bank's CEI/FECIFI declaration gateway where the transaction exceeds EUR 12,500; (5) complete RCS registration of the capital increase at the greffe du tribunal de commerce within one month before any disbursement, obtaining the filing certificate; (6) retain source-of-funds evidence including originator bank statements, board resolution and legalised corporate extract; (7) keep escrowed funds segregated from operational cash until the bank issues the blocked-account release ('déblocage') authorisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for steel-structure EPC treasury disbursements: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer over T2 (TARGET2) for EUR-denominated vendor payments within France and the EU, providing immediate finality and zero FX exposure; (ii) SWIFT MT103 T/T wires for non-EU suppliers (Turkey, China, Italy, Germany, Spain) with full remittance narrative, invoice reference and Banque de France trade-purpose classification; (iii) commercial import letters of credit under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700) covering heavy steel procurement, payable against compliant document sets comprising commercial invoice, negotiable bill of lading or CMR, mill test certificates per EN 10025, and inspection certificates, negotiated via the issuing and confirming banks; (iv) standby letters of credit (SWIFT MT760) for advance-payment guarantees, performance bonds and retention monies on prefabricated steel-shed EPC contracts; (v) in-bank cross-currency wires for EUR/USD conversion at spot rates executed within the same institution to eliminate corresponding-bank deduction risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/TRY, EUR/GBP) supported by genuine steel-procurement or prefab-sales underlying exposure
FX swaps (tom/next, spot-forward) for short-term liquidity conversion between EUR and USD operating accounts
Plain-vanilla European-style FX options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) for protected EPC bid and tender exposure
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR vs USD) on long-term project-finance borrowings with documented debt-service exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to non-convertible or thin-market currencies (onshore CNY, INR, TRY) solely against physical export or import underlying

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels) including directors' report, legal statements and, where applicable, statutory auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end; filing within 1 month after approval and in all cases before expiry of the 7th month after fiscal year-end (calendar-year SAS: by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice by registrar; court-ordered periodic penalty payments (astreinte); criminal fine up to €9,000 for the managing president; repeated non-filing for 12–24 months may trigger administrative strike-off and enhanced tax audit exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return package (Liasse fiscale) — Form 2065-SD plus supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For financial year ending 31 December: electronic filing due by 3 May of the following year; for non-calendar financial years: within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.4% per month; late-filing penalty equal to 10% of tax due (40% for intentional or abusive failure); automatic assessment if no return filed within 60 days after written notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business-premises levy declaration and payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises — CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — Local Public Finance Centre (Service des Impôts Partculiers/Professionnels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration (form 1447-C-SD) and payment due by 15 December of the taxation year for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% plus 0.5% per month interest; enforced by tax-collection authority through liens on assets; does not trigger corporate administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner register update / UBO formalities (event-driven; no separate annual confirmation in France if no change occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in the situation of the beneficial owner; record must be current as of each annual shareholder meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of €15,000 for natural persons and €75,000 for legal entities in case of intentional omission; simple negligence penalties of €5,000 and €25,000; potential prohibition from managing the company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for a French SAS when at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded at closing and continued over two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet assets above €4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax above €8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (ANC regulation 2014-03, Plan Comptable Général) for standalone statutory accounts; IFRS required only for consolidated financial statements of public-interest entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France maintains a dedicated RCS beneficial-owner register. A UBO declaration must be filed at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership. There is no stand-alone annual UBO declaration; nevertheless, the annual accounts filing and any share transfer trigger a maintenance review of the UBO register. The SAS president is responsible for ensuring that the registered data remains complete and accurate as of every annual shareholder meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registre des décisions de la direction)
Minute Book (Procès-verbaux des décisions et assemblées)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$180–US$2,400 per year for corporate domiciliation and registered-office services (Paris and major metropolitan areas at the upper end)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$14,000 for a standard statutory audit of a small or medium French SAS; complex steel-prefabrication structures may exceed US$20,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 50% of eligible expenses), innovation status benefits, and targeted preferential deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200A (Déclaration de résultat) via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the third month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 April for calendar-year entities)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-sourced revenue only where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Résultat avant impôt sur les sociétés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incorporate transfer pricing adjustments and economic substance compliance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Impôt sur les sociétés calculé
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply available tax credits or incentives
Ensure proper withholding treatment if applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.75% per month of delay on tax due, capped at 10% of tax due; willful evasion triggers criminal penalties including fines and imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% within EU/EEA; otherwise 12.8% reduced by applicable double tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain and submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to French tax authorities along with reduced withholding application
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to EU or under treaty; Interest: 0% to EU or under treaty (domestic rate 25%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50,000,000 EUR annual turnover for local file requirement
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require adequate substance for entities conducting activities in France; applies to holding companies and IP regimes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable income or overstating deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions: fines up to 5 million euros or 80% of annual turnover, imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil and criminal liability; possible disqualification from office, travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or provide TP documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 5 million euros or 80% of turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability with the company; potential personal fines

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French entity without sufficient economic substance or real business activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal sanctions including fines and possible imprisonment for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports or comply with KYC/AML obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 1 million euros or more, criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability, possible prison sentences, professional bans
